parsed_output.evidence: Root cause / sink: io.vertx.ext.web.handler.impl.StaticHandlerImpl.isFileExisting/getFileProps (StaticHandlerImpl.java:290-298, `fs.exists(file, resultHandler)` / `fs.props(file, resultHandler)`), where `file` is built at StaticHandlerImpl.java:610-611 (`getFile`: `webRoot + Utils.pathOffset(path, context)`) from the `path` sanitised at StaticHandlerImpl.java:131 (`HttpUtils.removeDots(URIDecoder.decodeURIComponent(context.normalisedPath(), false))`). Trust boundary crossed: attacker-controlled HTTP request path (via RoutingContext/HttpServerRequestWrapper) -> local filesystem read, with StaticHandlerImpl performing NO canonicalization/containment check of its own — the only defence is the string-level HttpUtils.removeDots() dot-segment stripper. removeDots() (vertx-core, io.vertx.core.http.impl.HttpUtils) only recognises '/' as a segment separator per RFC 3986 5.2.4; it does not recognise '\', which Windows/java.io.File on Windows also honours as a directory separator, so a request whose decoded path contains a percent-encoded backslash (e.g. `/..%5csecret.txt` -> decoded `/..\secret.txt`) reaches the sink with an un-neutralised ".." component and escapes the configured webRoot on any filesystem that treats '\' as a separator (CVE-2023-24815 class: "StaticHandler disclosure of classpath/filesystem resources on Windows"). All four traces in the alert converge on this exact same sink/root cause; they differ only in call-site/entry-point plumbing that a complete fix must cover: (1) direct route mount, includeHidden=true path (StaticHandlerImpl.java:189->292), (2) direct route mount, includeHidden=false path (StaticHandlerImpl.java:154->156->292), (3)/(4) same two variants reached through a RoutingContextDecorator-wrapped context (RoutingContextDecorator.java:180 normalisedPath() delegating to the same underlying RoutingContextImpl). Because the vulnerability's OS-level filesystem escape only manifests on Windows and this build/test container is Linux, the PoV cannot show an actual cross-directory file read via the OS; instead it captures — via a transparent, non-altering JDK dynamic proxy over the real Vertx/FileSystem interfaces — the literal, unmodified string value the real, unmodified StaticHandlerImpl.handle()/getFile() computed and handed to the real fs.exists() sink for a backslash-obfuscated traversal request, and verifies (java.nio.file.Path#normalize, an OS-neutral, deterministic arbiter) that this value still resolves outside webRoot. Verified empirically: on the current (unpatched) code the sink receives ".../webroot/..\secret.txt" (contains raw ".." after backslash, escapes webRoot) and the PoV exits 0; after applying the known upstream-equivalent fix (`.replace('\\','/')` before `removeDots` at StaticHandlerImpl.java:131) the sink instead receives ".../webroot/secret.txt" (confined to webRoot) and the same command exits 1.
parsed_output.expected_vulnerable_behavior: Sending an HTTP GET to a StaticHandler-backed route with a percent-encoded backslash traversal payload (`/..%5csecret.txt`, decoding to `/..\secret.txt`) causes the real StaticHandlerImpl to compute a backend file path (`webRoot + "/..\secret.txt"`) whose raw ".." segment was never stripped by HttpUtils.removeDots() and which resolves outside the configured webRoot once '\' is honoured as a path separator (true on Windows). The PoV observes this exact string as it is handed to the real FileSystem sink and, because it still contains an un-neutralised ".." that escapes webRoot, exits 0 to signal the vulnerability is present.
parsed_output.notes:
This PoV targets alert trace 1/3 (StaticHandler mounted directly via `router.route()`, includeHidden=true default, path via HttpServerRequestWrapper/RoutingContextImpl.normalisedPath() -> StaticHandlerImpl.java:131 -> :189/:192 getFile -> :290/:292 fs.exists sink). It was chosen as the primary trace because it is the shortest, most direct path to the shared root cause (the single `HttpUtils.removeDots(...)` sanitisation statement at StaticHandlerImpl.java:131) and requires no additional router-nesting scaffolding. Traces 2 and 4 (which route through RoutingContextDecorator.normalisedPath() at line 180, i.e. a StaticHandler mounted under a sub-router / decorated context) and the includeHidden=false branch (StaticHandlerImpl.java:154/156, exercised when `.setIncludeHidden(false)` is configured) reach the exact same sanitiser and sink and are NOT independently exercised by this PoV — a patch must fix the shared root cause (line 131 sanitisation, or equivalently Utils.pathOffset/getFile before line 611) rather than special-casing the direct-mount call site, or traces 2/4 will remain exploitable.

Technique used: the PoV runs the real, unmodified `io.vertx.ext.web.handler.StaticHandler` (production class) behind a real Vert.x HTTP server and Router, and sends a genuine HTTP request. To observe the tainted value at the sink without relying on actual OS-level path-separator behaviour (which only differs on Windows, not on this Linux container), it wraps the real `Vertx`/`FileSystem` objects in transparent JDK dynamic proxies (`java.lang.reflect.Proxy`) that delegate every call unchanged to the real implementation and only record the first argument of `FileSystem#exists`/`#props` calls — i.e., exactly the `file` value StaticHandlerImpl.java:292 passes to the sink. This avoids re-implementing/duplicating the sanitisation logic in the harness (which would not track a real patch to StaticHandlerImpl.java), while still working around the fact that Linux's java.io.File cannot physically demonstrate the Windows-specific directory escape. I verified this design against both the current vulnerable code (PoV exits 0) and a hand-applied version of the known upstream fix pattern (`.replace('\\','/')` before `removeDots` at line 131; PoV exits 1), confirming the command is patch-sensitive in the intended direction.

parsed_output.regression_hint: Invariant a correct fix must enforce: for ANY backend filesystem path StaticHandlerImpl derives from an HTTP request path (i.e., the value ultimately passed to `fs.exists(file,...)`/`fs.props(file,...)` in isFileExisting/getFileProps at StaticHandlerImpl.java:290-298), that path must remain lexically confined under the configured `webRoot` — no unresolved ".." (or platform-specific separator sequence that a target OS/filesystem would interpret as ".") may survive into the sink, regardless of which separator character was used to encode it in the request. Concretely, the sanitisation at StaticHandlerImpl.java:131 (or an equivalent containment check placed just before the sink) must neutralise backslash ('\') as a path separator — e.g. normalise '\' to '/' before/while running `HttpUtils.removeDots()` — and this must hold for every call site that reaches `getFile()`/`pathOffset()`, not just the one this PoV drives directly: (a) StaticHandlerImpl.java:154/156 (includeHidden=false branch), (b) StaticHandlerImpl.java:189/192 (includeHidden=true / default branch, exercised by this PoV), (c) requests reaching a StaticHandler mounted behind a `RoutingContextDecorator` (RoutingContextDecorator.java:180 normalisedPath()), and (d) the recursive `sendDirectory`->`sendStatic` index-page path (StaticHandlerImpl.java:264) which re-enters the same `getFile` sink with a server-derived (not purely request-derived) path segment appended. Known bypass variants a fix must also block, beyond the literal raw backslash used here: percent-encoded backslash (`%5c`/`%5C`, used by this PoV), double/mixed encoding (`%255c`), UTF-8/overlong encodings of backslash, mixed separators (`..\/`, `.\/.\/`), and any other input where a ".." component is separated from adjacent characters by something other than a bare '/' before reaching removeDots. Prefer fixing at the single shared choke point (the sanitisation statement feeding `path` in `handle()`, or a containment assertion added directly before the sink in `getFile`) over patching individual call sites, since all four alert traces — and the two call sites/entry points enumerated above — converge there.
parsed_output.summary: Created a real PoV (.security-pipeline/pov/PathTraversalPoV.java) for CWE-22 path traversal in vertx-web's StaticHandlerImpl (CVE-2023-24815-class Windows path-separator sanitisation bypass). The PoV runs the actual, unmodified StaticHandler/Router/Vertx production classes behind a real HTTP server, sends a GET request with a percent-encoded backslash traversal payload (/..%5csecret.txt), and — via non-altering JDK dynamic proxies over the real Vertx/FileSystem interfaces — captures the literal path string the real StaticHandlerImpl hands to the FileSystem sink (fs.exists at StaticHandlerImpl.java:292). It verifies that string still contains an un-neutralised '..' segment escaping the configured webRoot. Verified empirically: exits 0 against the current vulnerable code, and exits 1 after hand-applying the known upstream backslash-normalisation fix to StaticHandlerImpl.java:131 (then reverted, repo left clean).

parsed_output.patch_notes:
Root cause: StaticHandlerImpl.handle() (line 131) computes `path = HttpUtils.removeDots(URIDecoder.decodeURIComponent(context.normalisedPath(), false))`. removeDots() implements RFC 3986 5.2.4 dot-segment removal, which only recognises '/' as a segment separator. A request path containing a percent-encoded backslash (e.g. "/..%5csecret.txt") decodes to "/..\secret.txt"; the '..' is never recognised as a dot-segment (no '/' around it) so it passes through removeDots() untouched, then flows unchanged through getFile()/Utils.pathOffset() into `webRoot + path` and is handed to the FileSystem sink (fs.exists/fs.props). On a backend/filesystem that also treats '\\' as a directory separator (Windows), this resolves outside webRoot.

Fix: added `.replace('\\\\', '/')` on the decoded path immediately before it is passed to `HttpUtils.removeDots(...)` in handle(). This is the single point all four alert traces converge on (direct mount with includeHidden true/false, and RoutingContextDecorator-wrapped contexts all call context.normalisedPath() and funnel through this exact statement before reaching getFile()/pathOffset()/the sink), so the fix closes the root cause for every path, not just the PoV's direct-mount trace. It also blocks the wider bypass family described in the alert's regression_hint: raw '\\', percent-encoded '%5c'/'%5C', and any mixed-separator variant, since they all normalize to '/' before removeDots() runs.

Added two regression tests to StaticHandlerTest.java:
- testBackslashEncodedDirectorySeparatorIsNormalized: requests "/somedir%5cotherpage.html" and asserts it resolves to the real webroot/somedir/otherpage.html content (200). This is a genuine, OS-independent discriminator — verified failing (404) against the pre-patch code (backslash kept literal -> no file named "somedir\otherpage.html" exists) and passing after the fix.
- testBackslashEncodedTraversalIsBlocked: requests "/..%5csecret.txt" and asserts 404 (no leak). Note this assertion alone can't discriminate pre/post patch on a Linux CI runner (per the alert/exploiter's own analysis — the OS-level escape only manifests where '\\' is honoured as a separator, i.e. Windows), so it's kept as a basic safety/no-regression check alongside the discriminating test above rather than as sole proof.

Verified: full build (`mvn -B -DskipTests package` for vertx-web) succeeds; full StaticHandlerTest suite (65 tests) passes with the fix; confirmed testBackslashEncodedDirectorySeparatorIsNormalized fails on the unpatched source (stashed the source fix, kept the tests, reran) and passes once the fix is restored.
parsed_output.risk_notes: Low risk. The change only affects how request paths are sanitised inside StaticHandlerImpl.handle() before dot-segment removal; it does not change behavior for paths that don't contain a backslash, and the full existing StaticHandlerTest suite (65 tests covering caching, ranges, directory listing, hidden files, mount points, compression, etc.) passes unchanged. Because '\\' is not part of legitimate URL path syntax per RFC 3986 (it would only appear pre-encoded in a legitimate client request), converting it to '/' should not affect any legitimate client requests, only close off the traversal bypass. The provided POV exercises only one of the four traces in the alert (direct mount, includeHidden=true); this fix addresses the shared root cause so the includeHidden=false branch and RoutingContextDecorator-wrapped call sites are covered as well, per the alert's regression_hint and the exploiter's own note that a complete fix must not special-case the direct-mount call site.
parsed_output.summary: Fixed CWE-22 path traversal in vertx-web's StaticHandlerImpl (CVE-2023-24815-class Windows backslash-separator bypass): HttpUtils.removeDots() only recognizes '/' as a path separator, so a percent-encoded or literal backslash in the request path let a '..' segment survive sanitisation unmodified and could later escape webRoot on filesystems (e.g. Windows) that also treat '\\' as a directory separator. Patched the single shared choke point in StaticHandlerImpl.handle() (where context.normalisedPath() is decoded before removeDots() runs) to normalize '\\' to '/' first, so every alert trace — direct route mount with includeHidden=true or false, and requests reaching the handler through a RoutingContextDecorator-wrapped context — is sanitised identically and the traversal is neutralised before it ever reaches getFile()/pathOffset() and the fs.exists/fs.props sink.

parsed_output.diff_review: patch_only.diff touches exactly two files: StaticHandlerImpl.java (production fix) and StaticHandlerTest.java (two new regression tests). The fix is minimal and correctly targeted: `URIDecoder.decodeURIComponent(context.normalisedPath(), false)` now has `.replace('\\', '/')` appended before being passed to `HttpUtils.removeDots(...)`. Since removeDots() only recognizes '/' as a segment separator (RFC 3986 5.2.4) and ignores '\\', this was the exact root cause identified by the exploiter: a percent-encoded backslash ('%5c') let a '..' segment survive sanitisation untouched. Normalizing backslash to forward slash before removeDots() closes this for every call site that funnels through context.normalisedPath() -> handle() (direct mount with includeHidden true/false, and RoutingContextDecorator-wrapped contexts), matching all four alert traces since they share this exact statement. The two added tests (testBackslashEncodedDirectorySeparatorIsNormalized, testBackslashEncodedTraversalIsBlocked) are legitimate regression coverage, not a weakening of the PoV or test-only gaming — pov.diff (PathTraversalPoV.java) is untouched by the patch, confirming the fix wasn't tailored to dodge the specific PoV input. No unrelated or overly broad changes; risk of regressing legitimate requests is low since '\\' is not part of legitimate URL path syntax.
